findings.recommendation: Add per-route limiters (or a dedicated 'dangerous admin operations' limiter keyed by user+route) for bulk invite, bulk document ops, exports and organization delete; surface 429s in the admin UI and add tests.

findings.title: No undo/soft-delete is exercised despite the schema supporting it
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: columns dropped by 5302432 (925ec007) and hard-delete documented in ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md §3. NOTE: the previous register row said 'still open — columns exist' at 9c0b88c, which was already false at that commit (the drop landed 2026-10-02, before 9c0b88c); the previous note was stale/incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hard-delete decision documented in operator docs; if soft delete is ever revisited it must be end-to-end (writes set deleted_at, reads+RLS filter, restore UI).

findings.title: Approval flows allow self-approval and cancellation of already-approved requests
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d (approval-flows special check).
findings.recommendation: Reject approve/reject when the actor is the requester (configurable, at minimum for privileged request types); restrict cancel to pending requests (or record a reversal event with reason); add tests for both.

findings.title: Destructive deletes are not consistently audit-logged
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d (audit-log special check).
findings.recommendation: Add logAuditEvent to the seven missing DELETE handlers (or a shared audited-delete helper), and add a CI/test guard that every router.delete handler either logs an audit event or is explicitly exempted.

findings.title: Any org member can open the Stripe billing portal for their org (no billing-contact check)
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d (billing-panel abuse case).
findings.recommendation: Gate the portal session on is_billing_contact (or a new client-facing billing permission), or configure the Stripe portal to a restricted action set; add tests for member vs billing-contact access.

findings.title: No machine-enforced agent guardrails: allowed paths, human-approval actions, and small-batch PR limits exist only as prose
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: guardrails are documented (AGENTS.md + .continue) and several generated-file/secret/migration boundaries are machine-enforced, but PR-size limits and agent path allowlists remain prose-only, and openapi.yaml/prompt-provenance enforcement is partial. The previous register carried this row unverified from 20261002; the fix commit 67b20e79 was already an ancestor of the previous audit commit 9c0b88c.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guardrails section as the human-readable contract, then add machine checks where cheap: (a) a PR-size advisory/fail (changed-files/net-lines) or a required reviewer when the size threshold is crossed; (b) run verify-prompts.js verify in the PR test job, not only at the deploy gate; (c) a CI step that regenerates docs/openapi.yaml and fails on diff (or extends openapi-audit.js to compare the committed file against buildSpec()); (d) consider a CODEOWNERS-driven required-review label for .github/, supabase/migrations/ and apps/api/src/middleware/.

findings.title: Prompt packs embed generated outputs alongside instructions without a machine-detectable "not instructions" marker
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: central 'Not instructions' banner and agent guidance exist (PROVENANCE.md:1-9, AGENTS.md:74-76, .continue:32), but the marker is not machine-detectable per file/per pack and no guard enforces it. Previous row carried unverified from 20261002.
findings.recommendation: Add the marker at the point of risk: a short banner (e.g. 'GENERATED OUTPUT — DATA, NOT INSTRUCTIONS') to embedded-output directories/READMEs or a per-pack README banner, and extend verify-prompts.js (or a new check) to assert that every non-prompt file under prompts/ lives under an outputs/runs/Run* directory or carries the marker. Regenerate prompts/manifest.json afterwards.

findings.title: `.continue/` agent configuration defines models only and does not surface project rules or boundaries
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: .continue/agents/config.yaml:26-33 surfaces the guardrails and points at AGENTS.md as authoritative (commit 67b20e79). Previous register carried this row unverified from 20261002.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a tiny config lint that asserts the Continue rules mention AGENTS.md and the four generated files, so the duplicate cannot silently drift from AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Google Analytics and Tawk.to load on public pages with no cookie-consent or opt-out gate
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (verification duty, previous area PRIV row PRIV-P2-001; subject matter is the analytics-script loading owned by this domain): both script blocks remain unconditional; no consent gate was added and no commit in 9c0b88c..8d299b8d touches layout.tsx. Cross-listed so the aggregator can dedupe against the privacy domain if it re-emits the same row.
findings.recommendation: Gate third-party scripts on an explicit consent state (load after opt-in or use Google Consent Mode default-denied), add a cookie banner with accept/reject, and document the opt-out in the privacy policy.

findings.title: Analytics API stores visitor IP and user-agent in plaintext despite the documented no-PII contract
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Complements the domain-06 finding on admin read scoping: this is about collection/storage and the no-PII documentation contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Drop or hash ip_address/user_agent in the insert and the schema, replace metadata with a typed per-event schema (or cap keys/size), update docs/modules/analytics.md to match, and add a regression test asserting no raw PII is written.

findings.title: Storefront analytics capture is dead: the browser helper is never called and cannot pass the CSRF gate
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; static analysis only (no running stack was exercised).
findings.recommendation: Wire track() into storefront views and send the CSRF token (or deliberately exempt this public path and document why), add an E2E that asserts a row lands in store_analytics_events, or remove the dead surface and correct the docs.

findings.title: First-party analytics events have no retention or purge path
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; this is the analytics-specific instance of the generic DATA-P2-006 'several stores lack a retention policy' row owned by the data domain.
findings.recommendation: Add a store_analytics_events retention task (e.g. 90-400 days, mirroring public-interaction-retention) or drop the PII columns, and document per-store retention in the privacy policy and the analytics module doc.

findings.title: Visitor-alert tracking collects IP/geo before consent and sends the visitor IP to ip-api.com over plaintext HTTP
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; the 90-day public_interactions retention (public-interaction-retention.ts) and bot filter (bot-detection.ts) are acknowledged mitigations, but they do not address consent or the cleartext transfer.
findings.recommendation: Use HTTPS for the geo lookup (or remove the third-party lookup), defer /public/init until consent is captured (or make the tracking explicitly consent-independent and document it), record consent server-side, and add a test that no pre-consent third-party call occurs.

findings.title: Mutations remain unguarded by `requirePermission` in several routers (including a governance state transition)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: governance submit + all five client-onboarding mutations are now guarded (commit 14a2b301, ancestor of HEAD); residual unguarded mutations remain in projects/ai/assets/findings/field-services and the mount-level guard test does not cover permissions — partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Extend requirePermission (or an explicit documented exception) to the residual mutating routes; extend route-authorization-guard.test.ts to assert a permission key on every mutating route outside a documented allowlist; add a dedicated limiter or documented intent for the public surfaces.

findings.title: External integration syncs report success while dropping items, and `jsm-sync` has no HTTP retry
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: jsm-sync pagination/retry/failure-reporting fix is present and tested (commit 1a6a5712, PR #150); jira-sync.ts:206 and stripe-reconcile.ts:146 still return ok:true after counting per-item errors — partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the jsm-sync result contract in jira-sync and stripe-reconcile: return { ok: false, error } when errors > 0 (or a structured partial result); retry 5xx in fetchJiraIssue; add unit tests injecting a failing per-item write.

findings.title: Published error-handling contract contradicts the implementation (codes, 422, and `request_id`)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: docs/API_ERROR_HANDLING.md was rewritten to the implemented contract (flat envelope, 400 VALIDATION, no 422, X-Request-ID header, real code vocabulary; commit a61aadc0 / PR #149) and each documented code exists in the code — verified-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Keep the doc in lockstep with error.ts when new codes are added; add the contract test asserting representative AppError/ZodError shapes.

findings.title: SDK retries unsafe requests without an `Idempotency-Key` (duplicate creates on transient failure)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the SDK sends a stable Idempotency-Key on unsafe requests (minted once per logical call) and the same key is asserted across retries (commit 08ad3d4d) — verified-fixed.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the same-key-across-retries regression test as new SDK methods are added.

findings.title: Outbound webhook dispatcher uses a non-atomic idempotency check (duplicate deliveries under concurrency)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both dispatchers use the atomic Redis SET NX claim (in-memory fallback) and release on failure, with concurrent-duplicate collapse covered by tests (commit d5e0d5b7, stranded remediation on main) — verified-fixed.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the concurrency regression tests when the dispatcher is refactored.

findings.title: Search falls through to an unscoped cross-tenant query
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: routes/search.ts scopes every query to req.orgScope and substitutes ["__none__"] on an empty scope; search-tenant-scope.test.ts asserts the fail-closed behaviour — verified-fixed (ledger a97425d status carries).
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the fail-closed test as new search surfaces are added.

findings.title: OpenAPI schema is public and the Swagger UI is blocked by CSP
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: routes/docs.ts 404s in production and the nonce/SRI wiring is covered by docs.test.ts — verified-fixed (ledger a97425d status carries).
findings.recommendation: None required.

findings.title: Single-droplet, single-instance runtime is a hard SPOF
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: platform failure/recovery runbooks present and extended; topology unchanged (single droplet, single instance, single Redis) and the deploy is still stop-the-world — status stays partially-fixed. Owner/budget decision.
findings.recommendation: Keep the runbooks. Budget a second droplet or at minimum a documented blue/green or `up -d` without `down` deploy path to remove the per-deploy outage; state the availability target and the deploy downtime window in docs/SLO.md. Redis remains a shared SPOF (see the shared-Redis finding).

findings.title: API defaults to the service-role DB client (RLS bypass)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: fail-closed startup guard and metric wiring present (rls-startup-check.ts, portal_rls_bypass_total); the default remains the service-role client and the per-module rollout is operational/owner-gated — status stays partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Record the deployed allow-list contents and date in docs/RLS-rollout.md (or emit it as a startup log line) so the rollout state is reviewable; extend the rollout to the remaining write paths; keep the IR-P1-006 bypass metrics and MCTTenantScopeRegression rule as the runtime backstop.

findings.title: Prometheus loads rules but has no alert routing
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: Prometheus alerting block + Alertmanager service + watchdog receiver are all present in the as-built compose; deploy fails closed in prod without the watchdog URL. Still fixed.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Keep the watchdog URL + basic-auth secrets provisioned per environment and re-run the IR-P0-003 fail-closed check on every prod deploy (already enforced).

findings.title: API always enqueues to BullMQ while the worker backend is a separate setting with no parity check
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Adjacent to RES-P2-003 (worker refuses inline in prod, verified-fixed) and RES-P3-003 (AGENTS.md queue-backend doc gap, open) but distinct: this is the API/worker producer-consumer contract, which remains unchecked.
findings.recommendation: Give the API the same QUEUE_BACKEND contract and fail closed on a producer/consumer mismatch (or derive both from one deployment value); add a startup/health assertion that a test task enqueued by the API is observed by the worker; document the coupling in the deployment docs.

findings.title: One non-replicated Redis backs queue, cache, idempotency and scan locks; failure degrades silently
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Related to the single-droplet SPOF row but a distinct failure mode (semantics change, not just availability).
findings.recommendation: Separate the queue from the cache (or enable Redis persistence/replication) and raise the memory cap; make idempotency degrade loudly (metric + alert) rather than silently, and document the degraded-mode semantics in the failure runbooks; add a Prometheus alert on Redis OOM/eviction and queue depth (worker_task_queue_depth is exported but has no rule).

findings.title: No refund and incomplete trial/cancel state handling
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the refund half is fixed (e3a14b5b, present at 9c0b88c); trial/cancel lifecycle fields and dispute/credit-note coverage remain missing.
findings.recommendation: Add trial_start/trial_end/cancel_at_period_end/canceled_at/interval to subscriptions and persist them in webhook + sync upserts; store refund amount/date; handle charge.dispute.* and credit_note.* if refunds/disputes matter to finance.

findings.title: `POST /billing/sync` does not paginate Stripe results
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: unchanged since the 20261002 finding; the silent partial-failure behavior is additionally documented in the evidence above.
findings.recommendation: Loop on has_more/starting_after (bounded), report per-object synced/error counts, and return a non-2xx or explicit errors[] when any Stripe call fails.

findings.title: Reconciliation job has no drift detection, alerting, or tests
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still suspend-only, still no drift metrics/alerting/tests; the job reports ok:true on partial failure.
findings.recommendation: Emit drift metrics (per-org subscription status mismatch, invoice/payment counts and sums), write fetched Stripe state back to the mirror, return failure when errors>0, alert on drift/failure, and add tests for terminal vs past_due suspension and partial failures.

findings.title: Failed payments produce no notification or dunning visibility
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: unchanged since the 20261002 finding; no billing notification producer and no dunning UI.
findings.recommendation: Create a billing-module notification (plus optional email) on invoice.payment_failed with a link to the Stripe portal, and surface a past-due banner on the portal billing page.

findings.title: Subscription/invoice schema lacks trial, interval, and void-lifecycle fields
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: void/uncollectible statuses are now ingested (fix landed in e3a14b5b); trial/interval columns and void timestamps still absent.
findings.recommendation: Add interval, trial_start, trial_end, cancel_at_period_end (and quantity/seat count) to subscriptions; add voided_at to invoices; populate from webhook + sync.

findings.title: Stripe webhook DB writes ignore errors and still mark the event processed
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; closely related to BILL-P2-003 (no drift detection/alerting).
findings.recommendation: Check every Supabase write result; log and throw (or record a failed delivery metric) on error so the claim is released and Stripe retries; optionally add a dead-letter/reprocess path.

findings.title: Out-of-order or late-retried Stripe events can overwrite terminal payment states
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; Stripe delivery ordering across objects is not guaranteed and retries can arrive after the 24h claim TTL.
findings.recommendation: Make payment status monotonic (never downgrade refunded/partially_refunded), or compare event.created/updated before writing; treat refunded/voided as terminal states in the upsert.

findings.title: Billing read endpoints fall back to all-tenant scope for cross-tenant roles without an admin-scope guard or audit
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the web UI always sends organization_id, so the gap is reachable via direct API/SDK use.
findings.recommendation: Adopt resolveAdminTenantScope + applyOrgScope/applyRequestedOrg on the billing GETs (fail closed for empty scope) and audit implicit cross-tenant reads.

findings.title: `require_code_owner_reviews:false` makes the committed CODEOWNERS advisory only
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both JSON files set require_code_owner_reviews true (8b02f91a). The 20261004 register carried this row as open/unverified; the committed fix predates that run. Residual: live application and team membership are not verifiable from the repository (Unknown).
findings.recommendation: Apply the JSON to GitHub; verify each @mainecybertech/* team exists and has members (cannot be checked from the repo); add a CODEOWNERS validator (see the CODEOWNERS-validation finding).

findings.title: No break-glass / bypass process for branch protection, and no bypass audit trail
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: no break-glass/emergency-merge procedure exists for repository protection; unchanged since 20261002-0344.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/RUNBOOK_EMERGENCY_MERGE.md: trigger conditions, incident ticket reference, named approver (owner), time-box, exact steps, mandatory post-incident review; record each bypass from the GitHub audit log (`gh api /orgs/{org}/audit-log` filtered to protected_branch events) in the incident. Consider GitHub Rulesets with an explicit bypass-actor list so bypasses are attributed and logged.

findings.title: No drift detection between committed branch-protection JSON and live GitHub settings
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still no live-drift automation; unchanged since 20261002-0344. The new check-required-checks guard is static only.
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled (weekly) + workflow_dispatch drift job that fetches `branches/{main,develop}/protection`, normalizes it to the committed JSON shape, and fails on diff (store both as artifacts); a token with administration:read is required (default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read protection). Optionally open an issue or PR with the live state.

findings.title: Path-filtered required checks can leave `main`/`develop` protected by checks that never run
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: test/lint/typecheck are unfiltered (fix present), but e2e remains path-filtered while required on main. Previous register marked this verified-fixed based on test.yml only; the e2e residual was not checked.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `paths:` filter from e2e.yml's pull_request trigger (matching test/lint/typecheck), or add an always-running companion job that reports success when the real suite is intentionally skipped. Update docs/CI.md:132-135 to state that E2E is required on main and unfiltered. A CI test should assert that every context in *.json comes from a workflow whose pull_request trigger has no paths filter.

findings.title: Required-check guard is not run on pull requests or on branch-protection-only changes
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: the control added by 8b02f91a is real but is only reachable through the deploy gate, not the PR that changes the protected-check list.
findings.recommendation: Run `node scripts/check-required-checks.mjs` in the PR gate (a step in test.yml, or add it to the unit-tests composite used by both test.yml and validate.yml), and/or add `.github/branch-protection/**` to a validate trigger. Document the script in scripts/README.md.

findings.title: `deploy-do` manual dispatch can target prod from an arbitrary ref, bypassing the develop->main promotion model
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; related operator-gated residual tracked as CI-P1-001 (reviewer configuration).
findings.recommendation: Fail the setup job when deploy_target=prod and github.ref != refs/heads/main (with an explicit, logged owner override if needed), or move prod dispatch to a separate workflow restricted to main; ensure prod-approval reviewers are configured and test the pause.

findings.title: Security scan jobs are not required checks, so failing scans do not block merges
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Live CodeQL enforcement (ruleset 'code scanning results') cannot be verified from the repo — mark that part Unknown.
findings.recommendation: Add the security contexts (Test / security-scan, Test / secrets-scan, and the CodeQL analyze check) to the required lists, or adopt a GitHub Ruleset with 'Require code scanning results'; otherwise correct docs/CI.md's Gate column to 'Best-effort/alerting'. Verify the live ruleset state when applying protection.

findings.title: Intra-tenant capability escalation via unguarded mutations
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: governance + all five client-onboarding mutations are guarded; residual unguarded mutations remain in projects/ai/assets/findings/field-services, and a new role-assignment escalation path (P1) supersedes the old 'unguarded mutation' route.
findings.recommendation: Extend requirePermission (or a documented exception) to the residual mutating routes; extend route-authorization-guard.test.ts to assert a permission key on every mutating route; close the role-assignment gap with a central assertCanAssignRole.

findings.title: Definer RPC identity trust composes into forged approvals/comments
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5302435 enforces caller identity for end users; unchanged since the 9c0b88c verification.
findings.recommendation: None required. Add a DB-level regression test asserting a user-scoped call with a foreign p_user_id raises, and keep the service-role path covered by an API test.

findings.title: RLS admin-gate regression composes with the API trust model into MSP admin denials
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5302436 restores the platform-admin key set on the four regressed DELETE policies; unchanged since the 9c0b88c verification.
findings.recommendation: None required for these four gates. Add a static drift check that any admin-gate policy created after 5302436 uses user_has_role with the shared key list, so the literal-list regression cannot recur.

findings.title: Retention + cascade compose into silent destruction of audit evidence
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5302108 cascade and the no-archive purge are unchanged (DATA-P2-005 still-open); the composition remains open.
findings.recommendation: Write audit rows to an archive sink before org deletion and before the 365-day purge, or change the FK to on delete set null and archive on retention; record the decision in the data-governance docs.

findings.title: Internet-open SSH composes into service-role exfiltration and tenant takeover
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: code fail-closed (variables.tf:76-92, terraform-do.yml:98-110); live droplet state not verifiable read-only — the composition is closed in code, not evidenced in production.
findings.recommendation: Operator: set secrets.ADMIN_IP_RANGES to the office/VPN CIDRs and run terraform-do apply; then verify SSH is unreachable from the public internet and record it. Consider moving long-lived secrets off the droplet (e.g. instance-scoped short-lived credentials).

findings.title: Terraform version/lockfile conflict composes into un-gated infrastructure change
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: providers.tf >= 1.15 and all pins 1.15.9 (47a5685d, ancestor of main); lockfile consistent — the 'regressed' claim is not reproducible for the version/lockfile half. The un-gated infrastructure-change half remains (terraform-do manual-only; prod-approval reviewers unset).
findings.recommendation: None for the version conflict. For the un-gated half: configure prod-approval required reviewers (shared with CHAIN-P1-008) and re-enable the weekly drift plan; consider a plan-required CI check for terraform changes once the DO token is rotated.

findings.title: Silent worker failures + in-stack monitoring compose into undetected degradation
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: worker liveness and deploy-time health are now detected (MCTServiceDown, Watchdog, fatal deploy health check); task-level failure/DLQ remains unalerted and the single-Redis silent degradation is new evidence (02 domain P2 open).
findings.recommendation: Add an alert on the webhook/DLQ counters and on BullMQ failed-job counts; give generic tasks a dead-letter path; make Redis degradation loud (metric + alert) rather than silently changing semantics; document the degraded-mode semantics.

findings.title: Decorative API-key permissions compose into over-privileged, RLS-bypassing machine credentials
findings.note: new chain at 8d299b8d; composes SEC-P2-xxx (API-key scopes never enforced) with the service-role default client. Static-walk supported.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the intersection of req.apiKey.permissions with the resolved permissions in requirePermission (checking req.apiKey), or remove the column/display and document that keys always inherit the creator's permissions; add permissions to the create schema + admin UI if scoping is intended. Require a permission on GET /api-keys and document the service-role behavior for keys.

findings.title: Unclaimed webhook retries and dedup gaps compose into duplicate outbound deliveries
findings.note: new chain at 8d299b8d; composes WH-P2-xxx (webhook-retry has no row claim), NOTIF-P2-xxx (API email not gated on dedup), and the single-Redis degradation finding (02 P2). Static-walk supported.
findings.recommendation: Claim each row atomically before sending (UPDATE ... SET next_retry_at = lease WHERE id=? AND retry_count=? / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and/or claim the delivery idempotency key in the retry path; skip the email in notifyAndEmail when inApp.deduped is true (mirroring claimNotificationEmail); make Redis-degraded idempotency loud (metric + alert). Add a concurrency test with two overlapping webhookRetry calls.

findings.title: Guard-then-fetch worker monitoring composes into droplet-internal SSRF
findings.note: new chain at 8d299b8d; composes SEC-P2-xxx (worker monitoring guard-then-fetch TOCTOU) with the single-droplet co-location topology. Static-walk supported; not reproduced with a live rebinding host.
findings.recommendation: Route uptime/website checks through pinnedFetch (or an equivalent pinned dispatcher) and pin the TLS socket in fetchSslExpiry to the validated address; share one SSRF/pinned-fetch module between apps/api and apps/worker so the guard cannot drift per call site. Add a regression test with a rebinding resolver.

findings.title: World-open DigitalOcean firewall mutation with no approval and unvalidated udp_port

findings.title: Production approval environment documented as having no required reviewers

findings.recommendation: No further doc change; close when CI-P1-001/CI-P1-003 are provisioned.

findings.title: DB restore test reports success without asserting restore integrity
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: assertion step present and fail-closed (DR-P0-002 / IR-P1-004 fixes).
findings.recommendation: No code change required; keep the baseline in sync with migrations (the file documents this).

findings.recommendation: Operator: rotate DO_API_TOKEN, set TF_DRIFT_PLAN_ENABLED=true, then re-enable a PR/push plan trigger (plan-only; apply stays input-gated) so infra changes get a reviewable plan.

findings.title: Chromatic visual-regression job is permanently non-blocking
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: continue-on-error: true still present (chromatic.yml:28); not re-checked previously (was carried open from run 20261002).

findings.title: Empty METRICS_TOKEN has no deploy guard and is documented as optional; it breaks the API scrape and fires a false service-down alert

findings.title: Alert delivery and the dead-man's switch are configured but never exercised end-to-end; no monitoring-of-monitoring rules

findings.title: Container logs are not persisted off-box and are destroyed by the deploy's `compose down`

findings.title: No repository evidence of external uptime checks for platform endpoints; an edge/proxy failure is undetected in-stack

findings.title: docs/audits/README.md documents a run contract that contradicts the pack and the actual runs, and its Runs table omits all three repo-deep-dive runs

findings.title: Request metrics label uses the raw URL path, so Prometheus cardinality grows with every resource ID
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Static analysis only; cardinality not measured against the live Prometheus.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the label to the matched route template (e.g. compute the label in a middleware that runs after routing, or map req.path with a normalizer that replaces UUID/numeric segments and unknown paths with a bounded bucket), then add a recording/alert rule on prometheus_tsdb_head_series and a test asserting the label set stays bounded.

findings.title: Public storefront pages are force-dynamic and uncached; each page view costs two Supabase reads
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Either add responseCache(60..300) to the public catalog routes (and invalidate on admin catalog writes), or switch the public store pages from force-dynamic to ISR (export const revalidate = 300) with on-demand revalidation after catalog edits. Add a test that a second page request is served from cache (X-Cache: HIT / static build).

findings.title: resolveEffectivePermissions is uncached and fans out 4–6 queries per gated request
findings.note: Verification of previous row SEC-P3-005 (area SEC, subject matter caching/query fan-out). re-verified at 8d299b8d: still uncached, and the 211 call sites / 44 files + double resolution via requireEntitlement quantify the impact. Severity re-rated P3→P2 for the PERF domain because it is a per-request fan-out on the majority of write endpoints; the SEC owner may keep its P3 security framing.
findings.recommendation: Add a short-TTL cache keyed by (userId, orgId) with explicit invalidation on membership/role/override writes, plus request-scoped memoization so requirePermission + requireEntitlement share one resolution. Mirror the existing entitlementCache pattern (entitlement.ts:48) and record cache hit/miss metrics.

findings.title: Bulk invite performs 4 sequential Supabase calls per invite and cannot finish 500 invites inside the 30s request timeout
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Latency not measured (static analysis); the 30s timeout vs 4 sequential calls × 500 entries is structural.
findings.recommendation: Cap the synchronous batch (e.g. 25-50) and enqueue the rest as a worker task, or batch the profile/membership lookups with .in() and create users with bounded concurrency; return a job id and progress. Add a test that asserts the endpoint returns within budget for the max accepted batch.

findings.title: Each SSE notification stream opens its own Supabase Realtime channel with no connection cap
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Supabase Realtime plan quotas are external and not verifiable from the repo (Unknown); the per-connection channel design is confirmed in code.
findings.recommendation: Use one shared server-side subscription/fan-out (e.g. a single Postgres change listener or Redis pub/sub) and broadcast to local SSE clients, cap concurrent streams per process, add jittered reconnect backoff on the client, and fix the polling-fallback cleanup. Load-test with a few hundred concurrent EventSource clients before enabling RLS_READS_ENABLED for notifications.

findings.title: POST /billing/sync does not paginate Stripe results
findings.note: Verification of previous row BILL-P2-002 (area BILL, subject matter pagination + third-party API cost, which is in PERF scope). re-verified at 8d299b8d: no pagination loop added; limits unchanged; upserts still sequential. Kept at the original P2 severity.
findings.recommendation: Page through Stripe with starting_after/auto-pagination until exhausted (report the page cap as a failure, mirroring the jsm-sync fix), and batch the Supabase upserts (single multi-row upsert or a bounded-concurrency helper).

findings.title: Google Analytics and Tawk.to load on public pages with no cookie-consent or opt-out gate
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (previous row PRIV-P2-001, open at 9c0b88c): layout.tsx:58-78 still injects GA and Tawk.to unconditionally and no consent/cookie component exists anywhere in apps/web. Analytics-domain sibling AN-P3-001 (no Consent Mode signalling) is owned by 39_analytics_tracking_privacy — do not duplicate there.
findings.recommendation: Gate GA/Tawk.to behind a consent manager: default-deny (Google Consent Mode v2 with analytics_storage denied by default), load the Tawk.to script only after opt-in, persist the choice, and expose a visible opt-out. Add a cookie table to the privacy page.

findings.title: Consent is captured only in the browser and never recorded or enforced server-side; the store quote form collects PII with no consent at all

findings.title: Published retention statement (three years) contradicts the 90-day contact-form PII purge

findings.recommendation: Either align the policy text to the enforced 90-day platform purge (and state the retention of the Teams/JSM copies separately), or change the purge window to the published period. Add the platform retention schedule to docs and reference it from the policy.

findings.title: Audit-log PII redaction is a shallow key-name filter; person names and job titles are persisted for 365 days
findings.note: new finding this run. Related but distinct from SEARCH-P2-002 (raw search terms, verified-fixed) and ADMIN-P2-004 (destructive deletes not audit-logged, open).

findings.title: No data-subject access/export/erasure path or DSAR runbook; offboarding never removes profile or auth records
findings.note: new finding this run. Complements the open ADMIN-P2-002 (org delete unrecoverable) but is about the individual data-subject lifecycle, which no domain currently covers.
findings.recommendation: Add an operator runbook for DSAR handling (identity verification, export query set, erasure/anonymisation steps, response clock), implement an admin-triggered account deletion/anonymisation path (Supabase auth.admin.deleteUser + profile scrub), and record the procedure in docs.

findings.title: Visitor IP addresses are sent to ip-api.com over plaintext HTTP for geolocation
findings.note: new finding this run.
findings.recommendation: Use an HTTPS-capable geolocation provider (or ip-api's paid HTTPS endpoint), or perform geo lookups only after consent; document the vendor and retention in the subprocessor list.

findings.title: Privacy governance documentation set is missing and the published vendor list omits processors used in code

findings.recommendation: Create docs/PRIVACY.md (classification + retention schedule + DSAR pointer), docs/SUBPROCESSORS.md (vendor, purpose, data categories, region, DPA status), and a tenant-facing DPA template; link them from the privacy page and SECURITY.md.

findings.title: Inbound webhook handlers ACK 200 while ignoring persistence errors, dropping events during DB degradation

findings.title: Worker queue degradation is invisible to health checks and alerting

Add a chaos test that stops Redis and asserts the alert fires.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown is not effective in production: Redis handles are never closed and Docker's 10s stop timeout kills the worker before its 30s drain budget
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Complements RES-P3-001 (watchdog present = verified-fixed); the watchdog cannot help when Docker SIGKILLs first.
findings.recommendation: Set stop_grace_period (>= WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS, e.g. 60s) on the worker and API services; close scan-lock/idempotency/producer connections during drain and exit(0) explicitly on a clean drain; add an integration test that SIGTERMs mid-task and asserts a clean exit and no duplicate side effect.

findings.title: Deploys are stop-the-world: `docker compose down` before `up` takes the whole stack offline with no rolling replace
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Cross-domain: deploy topology is owned by INFRA, but the failure mode (planned outage + no rolling replace) is resilience; no previous register row covers it.

findings.title: webhook_dead_letters has no user-scoped DELETE policy while the API deletes via the RLS client

findings.title: document_versions UPDATE policy still uses the raw unfiltered membership predicate

findings.title: store_quotes public INSERT policy allows arbitrary organization_id after tenant scoping

Add a behavioral test: authenticated user inserts with a foreign organization_id => denied.

findings.title: Notification surfaces swallow failures: preferences save silently fails and a failed list load renders a false empty state
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. NOTIF-P1-001 (preference enforcement) was re-verified fixed at 9c0b88c and is owned by domain 30; this finding is only about the UI feedback.
findings.recommendation: Show an inline error + retry on load and save failure; only show the empty state when the load succeeded; align the copy with the save-button model.

findings.title: NotificationBell SSE fallback leaks a 30-second polling interval per component instance
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Store the interval id in a ref and clear it in the effect cleanup (and before starting a new one); or replace SSE with a reconnect-with-backoff + single poller.

findings.title: Client-onboarding create swallows the redirect: success shows a cryptic error and invites duplicate records
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Rethrow redirect errors (or move redirect outside the try/catch) as done elsewhere; add a test that asserts navigation after create.

findings.title: Onboarding checklist items cannot be completed anywhere in the web app
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Wire the checklist PATCH into the portal/admin onboarding detail (checkbox + notes + completed_by), or seed items and provide an admin completion control.

findings.title: Session/MFA expiry has no user-facing explanation and the ?mfa=required step-up redirect is ignored
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Add ?reason=expired copy on /login and a visible 'Verify to continue' step-up banner (challenge+verify for any verified factor) when ?mfa=required is present.

findings.title: Privileged membership/approval actions lack confirmation and success feedback (suspend/reject are one click)
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Overlaps thematically with domain 26's destructive-action rows but is a distinct (membership/access) workflow.
findings.recommendation: Use ConfirmDialog for status transitions that remove access, and return a success/error result rendered as a toast or inline message.

findings.title: Change Password form collects a Current Password it never checks and advertises a weaker rule than the API enforces
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. The 'current password not verified' aspect may also interest the security domain.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused field or actually verify it (Supabase reauth), display the real strength rules up front, and reuse one shared password-policy component on signup/reset/profile.

findings.title: Ticket-card bulk selection nests a checkbox and a status button inside a Link, so ticking a ticket also navigates
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Static review only (no browser run); click-bubbling behaviour is inferred from the missing preventDefault on the checkbox and its presence on the sibling button, and from the f0d79194 a11y commit that resized the same checkbox without catching the nesting.
findings.recommendation: Move the checkbox and the status control out of the Link (card as a div with a title-only link or a stretched-link overlay) or add an onClick that calls preventDefault/stopPropagation on the controls. Add a Playwright regression test that clicks the row checkbox and asserts the URL is unchanged and the selection count updates.

findings.title: Inline async action errors are not announced by assistive tech in ~44 components, contradicting the documented convention
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Count is a static heuristic (error state rendered in JSX with no live-region attribute in the surrounding block); a handful may announce through a parent region, so treat 44 as an upper bound.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a single InlineError primitive with role="alert" (or route action failures through useToast().pushToast('error', ...)), then sweep the ~44 call sites. Add a lint rule or code-review checklist item for new error renders.

findings.title: Several dialogs have no max-height or internal scroll, so tall forms are clipped on small viewports
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Verified statically: modal containers lack max-h/overflow-y while three other modals in the same app already implement it, so this is an inconsistency as much as a bug.
findings.recommendation: Add 'max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto' (or the overlay-scroll pattern) to every dialog, and fix the shared @mct/ui Dialog once so DocumentShareClient inherits it. Add a Playwright viewport test (e.g. 375x667) that opens each modal and asserts the submit button is visible.

findings.title: 89 of 319 pages have no page-specific title (79 dynamic detail pages + 10 static), so browser and AT titles are generic
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Counts from a static scan of page.tsx files (319 total); redirect-only pages among the 89 are not excluded from the count, but the sampled dynamic pages render real content.
findings.recommendation: Add generateMetadata to detail routes (ticket subject, asset/record name, org name) and explicit titles for the five auth pages. Add a test that walks the route table and asserts a non-default title per route (the existing scripts/check-docs-counts.mjs already parses route counts and could host the check).

findings.title: @mct/ui primitives are largely bypassed: 6 files import Button, 1 uses Input/Dialog/Badge, while the app hand-rolls 234 raw cyber-button* usages and four Chip copies
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Counts from grep over apps/web/app + apps/web/components; loading.tsx files legitimately use Skeleton, so the 'bypass' claim is about interactive primitives.
findings.recommendation: Pick one standard and enforce it: adopt Button/Input/Dialog in a pilot module and move Chip/ConfirmDialog/StatusPill into @mct/ui, or document that raw cyber-* utilities are the standard and delete the unused exports. Add a lint guard for new raw cyber-button* usages in new files.

findings.title: M365 inbound notifications have no enforced timestamp/replay window
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the 7-day atomic claim on the notification digest exists (mainecybertech#122), but logWebhookDelivery:47 storeIdempotencyKey resets the same key to the 24h default (idempotency.ts:50,144), so the effective window is 24h — residual documented.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the claim TTL when marking the key done — e.g. storeIdempotencyKey(key, "done", ttlSeconds) with the same M365 window (or use claimIdempotencyKey's value update), and extend the test to assert the final TTL after a successful M365 request.

findings.title: Inline dispatcher records a fixed `retry_count` and duplicates the worker's retry logic
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: actual attempt count and dead_letter marking present, single retry owner enforced — mainecybertech#129 (68fd8d12) now on main.
findings.recommendation: No action; keep the single-retry-owner rule when changing retry semantics.

findings.title: Outbound and DLQ delivery outcomes are not metered; only inbound success increments the counter
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: outbound success/failure + DLQ counters wired on API and worker paths (mainecybertech#129; metric registration IR-P2-001 at 36e5f723). Residual alerting is IR-P2-003.
findings.recommendation: Add a Prometheus rule on portal_webhook_dead_letters_total / failed-rate once alert thresholds are agreed.

findings.title: Inbound Jira/JSM signature falls back to re-serialized JSON when `req.rawBody` is absent
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: Jira/JSM require the captured raw body and fail closed (adea562c / mainecybertech#122, now on main).
findings.recommendation: No action; keep the fail-closed contract if the body parser is refactored.

findings.title: `webhook_dead_letters` has no DELETE policy while the API deletes via the RLS client
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still no DELETE policy for webhook_dead_letters (5302050 has select/insert/update only; 5302101/5302129 cover webhook_deliveries but not dead letters). Currently masked by the service-role default; breaks when webhook-management is added to RLS_WRITES_ENABLED. Sibling RLS-P2-002 — one fix closes both.
findings.recommendation: Add a DELETE policy mirroring the insert/update policy (webhooks:manage or admin-role scoped) in a new migration, and add an RLS-client test asserting the delete removes one row for a non-super-admin org admin.

findings.title: No per-provider payload schema or size cap on webhook ingress (global 10mb JSON limit)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still one global 10mb parser, no inbound schema validation, and webhook routes remain rate-limit exempt. No migration/route change since 9c0b88c.
findings.recommendation: Mount a tighter per-route JSON limit for /api/v1/webhooks/* (e.g. 256kb-1mb) and add per-provider Zod schemas that reject unknown/oversized payloads before side effects; consider a modest IP rate limit on inbound webhook paths.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint and delivery reads are available to any org member (not manage-gated)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (ACM-P2-005): reads still only require auth + org access while the webhooks:view permission exists; no requirePermission on any GET route.
findings.recommendation: Add requirePermission('webhooks', 'view') to the read routes (list, get, deliveries, dead-letters) and cover it in the route tests; consider redacting request_body/response_body for view-only callers.

findings.title: Webhook signing secrets are stored plaintext with no rotation or expiry
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (ACM-P2-007): secret is still plaintext text with no rotation/expiry metadata and no rotation inventory entry.
findings.recommendation: Document outbound endpoint secrets in SECRETS_ROTATION.md (90-day cadence, rotate via PATCH), add last_rotated_at + optional expiry and a rotation reminder, and consider encrypting the column at rest with FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

findings.title: Webhook SSRF guard has a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: pinnedFetch is used on all four outbound call sites (API dispatcher/test, worker dispatcher/retry); API pinned in #81, worker in 49646db7.
findings.recommendation: No action; add a regression test that a hostname re-resolving to 127.0.0.1 between guard and connect is still blocked.

findings.title: No alerting when webhook dead-letters accumulate or payment reconciliation drifts
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d for the webhook half of IR-P2-003: no alert rule consumes the DLQ/delivery counters. Payment-reconciliation half not assessed in this domain.
findings.recommendation: Add Prometheus rules: portal_webhook_dead_letters_total increase over 15-30m > 0 (warning) and sustained failure ratio > 50% (critical), routed via the existing Alertmanager receivers.

findings.title: Admin dead-letter retry of inline-dispatched failures no-ops and deletes the DLQ row
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: code-traced, no test covers the no-data retry branch (worker webhook-retry.test.ts:69-85 only covers empty/failed query).
findings.recommendation: Make retry truthful: keep the DLQ row until the retry task reports an actual attempt, and have webhook-retry re-insert a DLQ row (with a reason) when it skips a no-data row; alternatively have the inline dispatcher persist the replayable payload (or mark such rows as non-replayable and disable Retry in the UI).

findings.title: `webhook-retry` has no row claim: concurrent retry runs can double-send deliveries
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: worker retry task has no claim/lock; webhook-retry.test.ts:69-85 does not exercise concurrency.
findings.recommendation: Claim each row atomically before sending (UPDATE ... SET next_retry_at = now() + lease WHERE id = ? AND retry_count = ? / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), or claim the delivery idempotency key in the retry path; add a concurrency test with two overlapping webhookRetry calls.

findings.title: Client-side permission hiding is UI-only for several module actions
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: broad server-side enforcement confirmed by route scan (182 requirePermission call sites across 442 route definitions); residual exceptions and missing coverage gate documented.
findings.recommendation: Keep UI hiding as defense-in-depth and add the mutating-route guard-coverage CI test with an explicit allow-list after the ai/webhook gaps are resolved.

findings.title: No catalog-lint: referenced permission keys are not checked against the `permissions` table
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: no machine check exists. Code-side drift is currently zero, which makes the lint cheap to add (it would pass today) and it would also catch the RLS drift in ACM-P3-005.
findings.recommendation: Add permission-catalog.test.ts parsing requirePermission("a","b") and RLS user_has_permission(_, 'a','b') strings and asserting membership in the migration catalog; run it in CI.

findings.title: Public route surface is broad and has no single documented inventory
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: no single human-readable inventory; openapi.yaml marks public operations (partial mitigation) but the finding stands.
findings.recommendation: Generate a public-endpoints section from openapi.yaml (security: []) into docs, and add a test asserting every mutating route not on an allow-list is behind requireAuth.

findings.title: `GET /roles/:id` and `GET /me/permissions` are readable without an admin gate
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: GET /roles/:id carries requireAdmin (the named gap is closed); /me/permissions was already intended to be self-scoped.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for roles; keep /me/permissions self-scoped and covered by tests.

findings.title: RLS policies reference `manage` permissions that no role holds (dead predicates)
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: 10 distinct RLS-referenced keys remain undefined in the catalog (documents:manage 22 refs, projects:manage 17 refs). Not a live exposure — the clauses are inert — but a correctness/review hazard.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead clauses or add the intended permissions + grants deliberately; the catalog-lint test (ACM-P3-002) should cover RLS references so the set is machine-checked.

findings.title: `GET /api-keys` lists org keys for any org member (no `api-keys:view` gate)
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; same pattern as the still-open webhook read gate (ACM-P2-005).
findings.recommendation: Add requirePermission('api-keys','view') to GET / or document the accepted posture (mirrors ACM-P2-005 for webhooks).

findings.title: AI copilot endpoints have no permission gate (any org member can run summarization and reply drafts)
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; same action-gating family as ACM-P2-004.
findings.recommendation: Gate the copilot routes with requirePermission('ai','view') (reply-draft may warrant ai:create) or document the deliberate decision alongside the triage/analyze comment.

findings.title: Web admin gate accepts a broader role set than the API `requireAdmin` (guard/API divergence)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: divergence persists (8 web keys vs 2 API cross-tenant keys) but is now documented and API-enforced; severity stays P3.
findings.recommendation: Either align the web gate with the API admin tiers (or derive the portal role list from the API /me/permissions), or render read-only/403 states explicitly; add a test asserting the two key lists stay in sync.

findings.title: Active-org cookie setter performs no server-side authorization
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: setter still unguarded; risk bounded by API-side org-access enforcement + impersonation logging. No fix targeted at the setter itself.
findings.recommendation: Validate in setActiveOrg that the caller has an approved membership in the org (or is a platform admin) before writing the cookie; return a typed error otherwise.

findings.title: Admin global search and dashboard expose global resource names/counts to any admin
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: search and dashboard apply resolveAdminTenantScope/applyOrgScope with tests; fixed as part of the ADMIN-P1-001 hardening.
findings.recommendation: Keep the shared scope helper on all admin aggregate surfaces; add a regression test when new entities are added to search.

findings.title: Global store catalog is mutable by any tenant admin
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: catalog writes are org-pinned (MT-P0-003 fix) with explicit per-row ownership checks; global rows are cross-tenant-admin only.
findings.recommendation: Keep the org-pin helper for catalog writes; add tests covering cross-tenant product/category upsert and delete.

findings.title: Embedded repo maps and historical pack outputs still reference the pre-rename repository path
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: AGENTS.md/review.md path fixed and embedded outputs centrally labelled historical (PROVENANCE.md), but 52 occurrences remain, including a live onboarding tree (docs/ONBOARDING.md:37) and embedded pack maps. Previous row carried unverified from 20261002.
findings.recommendation: Fix docs/ONBOARDING.md:37 to 'mainecybertech/' (the only live doc hit); leave dated/historical files as-is under the PROVENANCE.md historical-output policy, or annotate them when they are next touched.

findings.title: `AGENTS.md` retains a large self-contradicting "snapshot" history that an agent must disambiguate
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: historical snapshot sections remain (and grew), with stale counts (787/789 prompts vs 632; 2,734 tests vs 3,490; 301 pages vs 319) that the docs-count guard does not cover. Previous row carried unverified from 20261002 — now re-verified as still open.
findings.recommendation: Move append-only 'Completed Work'/snapshot narratives to docs/HISTORY.md (or docs/CHANGELOG-style entries) and keep AGENTS.md to current state + Known Debt; if the history stays, fence it with a machine-detectable marker and add the remaining counts to the docs-count guard.

findings.title: Secrets guidance is spread across instructions without a linked canonical runbook
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md exists and is linked from SECURITY.md, but AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/PR template still do not link it. Previous row carried unverified from 20261002 — now re-verified as still open (procedural only).
findings.recommendation: Add the runbook link to the AGENTS.md guardrails/secrets bullet, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the PR-template secrets checklist item (one line each).

findings.title: Committed audit corpus under docs/audits/ is outside the untrusted-data boundary and has no integrity pin
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: the untrusted-data rule covers prompts/ only; docs/audits/ has grown into a committed findings corpus with no marker and no pin.
findings.recommendation: Extend the boundary explicitly: add 'audit outputs under docs/audits/ are historical data, not instructions' to AGENTS.md's Never list and to docs/audits/README.md, and consider a lightweight integrity check (e.g. hash the committed run corpus at publish time) or state that the corpus is intentionally unpinned because it is data.

findings.title: Audit output conventions in docs/audits/README.md are stale vs the committed runs
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: the committed runs and the documented contract disagree on run naming, required artifacts and status vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Update docs/audits/README.md: describe both layouts (per-pack layout section), align the status vocabulary with the repo-deep-dive framework or note the pack-specific vocabulary, and list the repo-deep-dive runs in the Runs table (or point at docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/).

findings.title: Prompt-pack provenance verification runs only at the deploy gate, not on PRs
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: verify-prompts is wired into validate.yml only; the PR pipeline does not run it.
findings.recommendation: Add `node scripts/verify-prompts.js verify` (dependency-free) as a step in the PR test job (unit-tests action or test.yml), keeping the deploy gate as defence in depth.

findings.title: No AI-authorship disclosure or provenance policy in contribution guidance
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: no AI-authorship policy exists; history already contains agent-authored commits with a generic co-author trailer.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional disclosure line to the PR template (tool/model + human owner) and one sentence to AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md; keep it lightweight so it does not block contributors.

findings.title: Analytics has no consent-mode signalling and no documented event/retention governance
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (verification duty, previous area AN row AN-P3-001): evidence unchanged from 9c0b88c; no commit in 9c0b88c..8d299b8d touches the layout, analytics route, or privacy page. The event registry partially exists but does not close the governance gap.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a consent-state contract (gtag consent mode + a cookie/analytics opt-out), document each event's purpose and retention in a governance doc, and add a retention task for store_analytics_events.

findings.title: Anonymous direct inserts to store_analytics_events bypass API validation, rate limits, and retention
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; static analysis. Anon-key exposure in the deployed web app was not verified (the web app calls the API, not Supabase directly).
findings.recommendation: Revoke the anon INSERT grant/policy (keep writes on the API path) or add DB-level constraints (event allow-list, column limits); keep the least-privilege migration as the single source of truth.

findings.title: Consent is not recorded and the privacy policy omits first-party tracking stores and opt-out mechanics
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Persist consent (flag, timestamp, policy version) on the interaction/lead record, add a cookie/analytics opt-out to the public site, and document the first-party tracking stores and their retention in the privacy policy.

findings.title: Error telemetry has no explicit PII scrubbing, retention, or vendor disclosure
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; the JS SDK defaults to sendDefaultPii:false, so exposure is not proven — this is a hardening/disclosure gap rather than a demonstrated leak. Session replay is absent, which is a strength.
findings.recommendation: Set sendDefaultPii:false explicitly, add a beforeSend scrubber for PII fields, document Sentry (and any other error processor) in the vendor list with retention, and add a test that error payloads drop email/phone/IP.

findings.title: Minor contract inconsistencies (`rateLimitByUser` non-enveloped 429, capped raw-array lists, no `request_id`)
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the X-Request-ID header is now emitted, but per-user 429, CSRF 403, idempotency 400/409 and timeout 408 are still non-enveloped, the rate-limiting doc still documents an enveloped 429, and the pagination helper is unused — partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Return failure("RATE_LIMIT", ..., 429) from all limiters, envelope CSRF/idempotency/timeout errors, align docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md, and either adopt or delete lib/pagination.ts while converting remaining raw capped arrays.

findings.title: OpenAPI artifact is not bound to a commit and the CI audit warns (not fails) on documented-but-missing routes
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the CI coverage gate now fails on missing routes and passes with 0 missing; commit binding, EXTRA allowlist and the stale AGENTS.md path count are still open — partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Embed the source commit (GIT_SHA) and generation date in docs/openapi.yaml; fail or allowlist EXTRA entries; update AGENTS.md:589 (and consider extending check-docs-counts.mjs to it).

findings.title: Realtime client has no reconnect path; server emits `auth_expired` with no documented client handling
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the client is unchanged — no reconnect, no auth_expired handling, and the polling fallback is not cleaned up on unmount — still-open.
findings.recommendation: Add an auth_expired listener (redirect to login) and bounded reconnect-with-backoff for onerror, close polling once reconnected, and clear the fallback interval in the effect cleanup; document the stream's disconnect contract.

findings.title: `/metrics` is fully public when `METRICS_TOKEN` is unset
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: /metrics is shared-token gated and 404s without METRICS_TOKEN — verified-fixed (ledger a97425d status carries).
findings.recommendation: None required.

findings.title: Batch Jira/JSM/M365 sync tasks are registered but never dispatched (no scheduler or enqueue path)
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.
findings.recommendation: Either add a scheduled scan with explicit per-tenant payload (project/organization) or an admin-triggered enqueue endpoint/runbook, and correct docs/JIRA_JSM_INTEGRATION.md to match the chosen dispatch model.

findings.title: M365 calendar sync recreates a calendar event for every task on each run (duplicate events, no idempotency)
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.
findings.recommendation: Persist the created Graph event id per task and PATCH it on re-sync, or send a stable transactionId and reconcile existing events before creating; add a re-run test asserting no duplicates.

findings.title: M365 inbound webhook acknowledges but only processes the first notification of a batch
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d (fresh audit); not present in the previous register.
findings.recommendation: Iterate value[] and dedupe/audit each notification (aggregate the response), or explicitly document why only the first is processed; add a multi-notification test.

findings.title: Web middleware gates routes on an unverified JWT `exp`
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: documented as a non-authoritative UX gate (apps/web/middleware.ts:5-16, commit 6ea9cb8e); behavior intentionally unchanged because the API verifies tokens — status stays partially-fixed.
findings.recommendation: Keep the comment and add a unit assertion that no page or server action reads authorization state from middleware; if a true edge gate is ever wanted, verify the signature in middleware or move to a signed session cookie.

findings.title: Architecture diagram and ADR 004 contradict the as-built runtime
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md overlap with INFRA-P2-005 is recorded; the diagram/ADR portion is architecture-domain.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md from the compose file and terraform; supersede ADR 004 with the Redis-backed cache decision; rewrite docs/PRODUCTION_VS_TESTING_DOMAINS.md for the droplet topology (overlaps INFRA-P2-005, owned by the infra domain).

findings.title: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` runtime override is inert for server-side code; docs claim internal SSR routing
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d. Validation step: `docker exec mct-portal-web-1 node -e "console.log(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL)"` is NOT sufficient (process env is set) — check the bundled server chunk or add a one-shot startup log of the URL actually used by getApiClient().
findings.recommendation: Read a server-only variable (e.g. API_INTERNAL_URL) at runtime for server-side code and keep NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL for the browser only; or correct the docs and remove the inert compose value. Validate by logging the resolved base URL from the running web container.

findings.title: Request timeout returns 408 but never cancels the handler
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Either thread an AbortSignal into handlers and abort downstream work, or document that the 408 is advisory only and require Idempotency-Key on mutating routes; add a regression test asserting a mutation after 408 is not applied twice.

findings.title: Worker metrics/health are unauthenticated while the API gates /metrics
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Gate the worker /metrics with the same METRICS_TOKEN check (or bind the metrics listener to a separate authenticated port) and add the authorization block to the Prometheus worker scrape; keep /health minimal.

findings.title: Webhook raw body typed as `string` but consumed as `Buffer`
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the Jira/JSM paths were hardened (rawBodyBuffer, fail-closed), but the Stripe path still casts a string to Buffer (app.ts:117 + webhooks.ts:153).
findings.recommendation: Capture req.rawBody as a Buffer (buf), type it consistently, and pass it to constructEvent without the cast; add a byte-mutation signature test.

findings.title: Billing email stored in plaintext and raw Stripe payment-method id rendered to users
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: unchanged; field encryption is still not applied to billing and both UIs render the raw payment-method id.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt billing_email with the existing field-encryption helper (or store it in the encrypted PII pattern), and display a card brand/last4 descriptor fetched from Stripe instead of the raw pm id.

findings.title: `invoice.paid` paid_at handling writes epoch dates (sync) or throws when status_transitions is missing (webhook)

findings.title: Web middleware gates routes on an unverified JWT `exp`
